The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
Why, in plain words: A software update took out the protection for shoppers who had bought nothing so far this month, so when a new account-page feature was switched on, the page's monthly spending calculation failed for those shoppers.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: 7m 0s {duration}
- Requests failing at the worst minute: 36.0% {peak_error_rate}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): 4,234.52 USD {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: did not roll back the deployment of io-shop - platform-unreachable, nothing was changed
- Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - confirmed, still in place
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #568 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Shoppers' account pages failed to load while monthly-spend-feature was on
Incident: HighErrorRate on io-shop
Date: Nov 12, 2026, 09:07 to 09:14 UTC
Status: Draft. 1 of 7 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 12, 2026, 09:19:17 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 12, 2026, 09:13:02 UTC
Ended by: Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - confirmed, still in place

Summary
The service broke at 09:07 UTC and was back to normal at 09:14 UTC, 7 minutes later. 27.4% of requests failed while it was broken, against 1.0% before it began. At its worst, 36.0% failed. The shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by 4,234.52 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. A software update took out the protection for shoppers who had bought nothing so far this month, so when a new account-page feature was switched on, the page's monthly spending calculation failed for those shoppers. What Argus did: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place. Argus did not test the first candidate it formed (C1): deployment-platform could not suspend the sync of `io-shop`: PATCH `/argocd/io-shop` was answered `503`: {"detail":"the deployment platform's API server is unavailable"}. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #568, for a person to review and merge. It was written against main, which does not contain the revision that ran: merged, it changes what runs only once a deploy carries it. Revision 383534e, which has no empty-month guard, was still running, so switching monthly-spend-feature back on would send account-page requests from shoppers with no purchases this month into the same division-by-zero failure.

Impact
7m 0s - onset until back to normal
36.0% - peak error rate
2,298 - requests failed
1.0% to 27.4% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (the rule's line is 10%)
4,234.52 USD - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
Revision 383534e removed the guard in average_spend_per_item_this_month that handled a shopper with no purchases this month. It also changed the function to decide 'this month' from each purchase's recorded_at. The function now divides the month's total by the number of purchases recorded this month with nothing to handle an empty month, so it raises ZeroDivisionError for any shopper with no purchase recorded this month.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account page requests failed with server errors, and the account page error rate rose well above its usual level.
  Evidence:
    G5309 ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 13 occurrences in 7 minutes, 09:07–09:13
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 35 occurrences in 37 minutes, 08:37–09:13; # was 0.50% to 36.00%, typically 1.00%, highest at 09:11
why 1 Account page requests failed because the spend summary raised a division-by-zero error inside average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py.
  Evidence:
    G5309
    S1 src/io_shop/spend_summary.py at 383534e
why 2 Requests reached that function because feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at P3. Flag evaluations went from all off before the onset, to a mix of off and on in the onset minute, to all on from the next minute. render_spend_summary sends a request to that function when the monthly summary is selected and the typical-spend rollout is not. The deploy of revision 383534e at P2 came at the same instant, so the record does not rule it out; the next step covers it.
  Evidence:
    P3 09:07:17 UTC flag toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
    G7e5d INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 evaluations - 30 occurrences in 30 minutes, 08:37–09:06
    G971b INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 72 / on 128 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 09:07
    Gce95 INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations - 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 09:08–09:13
    S1
  Ruled out:
    The earlier deploy of revision 65279ee (P1): with it in place, account pages were logged as rendering normally and the account page error rate was at its typical level before the onset.
      Gad41 INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 2 occurrences in 13 minutes, 08:42–08:54
      Gbac1
why 3 The flag sent requests into code that could not serve a shopper with no purchases this month: the revision deployed at P2 (read at T9 as running on every replica) had taken out the empty-month guard, so the function divides the month's total by the count of purchases recorded this month with nothing to handle a count of none.
  Evidence:
    P2 09:07:17 UTC deploy 383534e by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
    T9 09:13:08 Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run revision 383534e, deployed at 09:07:17
    D1 Deployment of revision 383534e to io-shop, compared against 65279ee - the revision deployed before it.
    S1
Contributing factors
- monthly-spend-feature was switched on at the same instant the revision carrying the changed code behind it was deployed. Most evaluations were already on in the onset minute and all were on from the next minute. No gradual ramp was seen. (AI-4)
- No test for a shopper with no purchases this month was seen in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py at the deployed revision. The change that removed the empty-month guard shipped without any seen check catching that the function now fails for that shopper. (AI-3)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | Revision 383534e, deployed 09:07:17 UTC and converged on all 3 replicas, changed average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. It removed the if not bought_this_month: return 0 guard and redefined "this month" from recorded_at. Accounts with no purchases this month now hit a ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47, and the account page error rate rose from about 1% to about 30%. | 0.55 | action not taken: deployment-platform could not suspend the sync of io-shop: PATCH /argocd/io-shop was answered 503: {"detail":"the deployment platform's API server is unavailable"}
C2 | Feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at 09:07:17 UTC, the same moment as the deploy. This sent traffic into the spend-summary path that raises ZeroDivisionError. The logs show evaluations moving from all off to 72 off / 128 on at 09:07, then all on. The flag alone is probably not enough, because the missing empty-month guard came from the deploy. | 0.40 | confirmed

Trigger
monthly-spend-feature flag went from OFF to ON at 09:07:17 UTC, by admin.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 09:13:23 | Did not roll back the deployment of io-shop for C1 | Argus | nothing to put back | platform-unreachable, nothing was changed
M2 | 09:13:23 | Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C2 | Argus | can be put back | confirmed, still in place
 | 09:16:42 | Proposed a fix: PR #568 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 09:07 UTC. HighErrorRate fired at 09:13 UTC, 6 minutes later.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature | mitigate | Argus | - | done
AI-2 | Review and merge the proposed fix | prevent | unassigned | PR #568 | open
AI-3 | Make the spend-summary tests, including a case for a shopper with no purchases this month, a required check that must pass before any change to src/io_shop/spend_summary.py can deploy. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Require flags that route traffic to new code paths, such as monthly-spend-feature, to be ramped up in steps, starting only after the deploy carrying the code has run healthy, rather than switched on for most traffic when the code deploys. | process | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Block monthly-spend-feature from being switched back on until a deployed revision carries the empty-month guard. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to page the on-call person. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-7 | Find out why the deployment platform's API server was unavailable during the incident, and restore a working rollback path for io-shop. | process | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
- 6 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent placed the start of the incident at 09:07.
- 23 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus moved on to C2.
- 23 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C2, moved from ON to OFF.
- 2 minutes 9 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent judged the action CONFIRMED.
- 3 minutes 42 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #568.
What went wrong
- The first action tried, rolling back the io-shop deployment, could not be taken: the deployment platform's API server was unavailable, which also put restarting, scaling and every other platform action out of reach.
- No on-call person was paged for the alert.
Where it got lucky
- The failing code path sat behind a feature flag that changed at the same moment as the deploy. Reverting the flag, which did not depend on the unreachable deployment platform, was enough to stop the errors.

Supporting information

What each deployment looked into changed
D1 | Deployment of revision 383534e to io-shop, compared against 65279ee - the revision deployed before it.
modified src/io_shop/spend_summary.py
  @@ -9,6 +9,8 @@
   
   from __future__ import annotations
   
  +from datetime import UTC, datetime
  +
   from io_shop.accounts import Account
   from io_shop.typical_spend import typical_spend_per_item
   
  @@ -41,14 +43,18 @@ def average_spend_per_item_this_month(account: Account) -> int:
       show what a shopper is spending now rather than what they averaged over
       three years.
   
  -    A shopper who has bought nothing this month averages zero, rather than
  -    dividing by an empty month.
  +    This month is decided from when the purchase was recorded rather than from
  +    the flag the writer set, so that a record which sat in a queue over a month
  +    boundary counts against the month it happened in.
       """
  +    now = datetime.now(UTC)
       bought_this_month = [
  -        purchase for purchase in account.purchases if purchase.in_current_month
  +        purchase
  +        for purchase in account.purchases
  +        if purchase.recorded_at is not None
  +        and purchase.recorded_at.month == now.month
  +        and purchase.recorded_at.year == now.year
       ]
  -    if not bought_this_month:
  -        return 0
       return account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month)
   
   
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault (as main has it). In src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, average_spend_per_item_this_month returns account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month). bought_this_month only holds purchases with in_current_month set. So for a shopper who has bought before but not this month, it raises ZeroDivisionError. The test file already calls that shopper "the ordinary case". render_spend_summary in the same file calls this function whenever use_monthly_summary is true and use_typical_spend is false. That is the branch the monthly-spend-feature flag selects.

Main vs. the deployed revision. Everything above is about main, which is the code I read. Revision 383534e isn't in main's history and I haven't read it. The investigation says the empty-month guard went missing in that deploy. Main has no guard either, so turning the flag back on against main would raise the same way.

The fix. If there were no purchases this month, the function now returns 0: nothing was spent this month, so nothing was spent per item. Shoppers who did buy this month take the same division as before.

The flag only decides whether a request reaches this function. The function is now safe whether the flag is on or off.

What stays the same. average_spend_per_item, the lifetime figure in the same file, is unchanged. It still raises ZeroDivisionError for an account with no purchases at all, which test_the_page_lets_a_failure_reach_its_caller expects.

The tests. tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py adds two cases for a shopper whose purchases all fall outside the current month:
• average_spend_per_item_this_month returns 0.
• render_spend_summary(..., use_monthly_summary=True) returns 0.

Against main as it stands, both would raise ZeroDivisionError. Nothing has run these tests yet.
What ran, read at the revision running when the alert fired

The document, by field:
overview: For {duration}, io-shop's account pages failed to load for shoppers who had not bought anything so far this month. At the worst minute, {peak_error_rate} of requests failed. The cause was a software update that removed a safeguard for these shoppers. When a new account-page feature was then switched on, the page's monthly spending calculation failed for them. Argus estimates the lost sales at {customer_loss}. Nobody was paged, and no on-call incident was linked to this one. Argus tried to roll back the io-shop software update, but it couldn't reach the platform, so nothing was changed. Argus then switched off the new monthly spending feature (the feature flag monthly-spend-feature). That change is confirmed and still in place. Argus has also proposed a permanent fix, PR #568, which is still a draft and has not been applied.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
